To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resting cells of the culture undergo a gradual development of their functional properties, which is reflected by a gradual increase in the length of their prereplicative periods and in the suppression of DNA-synthesis onset in the fused nuclei.
the longer cells stay quiescent the longer their prereplication period lasts, and the lesser is their fraction entering S-phase.

the longer the cells stay in a resting state before stimulation, the more difficult it is for them to enter the period of DNA synthesis, and that the nuclei of these cells suppress the entry of stimulated nuclei into the S-period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dependence of the entry of mouse fibroblast cells into a period DNA synthesis on the length of their preliminary resting period.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the dependence of the cell cycle progression on the duration of the resting state.
the study of the cell resting states and the mechanisms of the transition from resting to active states of cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cells are capable of changing their functional properties during their resting state.
the resting state is not an inert state, but a state of gradual transition of cell functions.

the resting cells go through a period of gradual changes, which are accompanied by changes in the ability to suppress the onset DNA synthesis in heterodikarions and in the ability to enter the S-period after stimulation, the changes increasing with the duration of the resting state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cells in a resting state can be characterized by a gradual decrease in their ability to proliferate, which is accompanied by the changes in the functional properties of their nuclei.
the resting cells are in a process of differentiation.
the resting period of cells is a period during which the cells gradually develop into cells that are more sensitive to stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration of the resting state of the cell is the main factor determining the length of its prereplicative period after the stimulation.
the duration of the prereplicative period of the cells is not only a function of the duration of the resting period, but also depends on the duration of the stimulation.
resting cells are not in a uniform state, but rather in a series of states with different properties, which may be called the resting cell cycle.
